I am farming yam and cassava on this my plot of about one hectare here in North Central. The soil is not as strong as before, so I must buy small fertilizer to help the tubers swell, and I still put the cow dung and household waste I gather during dry season. I use the cuttings and seed yams I kept from last harvest — the local ones do well here and I cannot afford these new hybrid seeds. My sons help me, but at heaping and harvest time I must hire small boys from the village because the work is too much for me at my age.
